validity:
Does the phrase between <target> tags refer, in this context, to a real-world occurrence, action, change, process, posture/state, or institutional act? An auxiliary word, entity, property, generic concept, hypothetical illustration, or action only inside a fictional work is not itself a real-world event mention. Actual reported speech or proposals can be events; do not assume their proposed actions occurred. Habitual action or a small incidental event may still be eventive. Do not judge its importance, admission eligibility, truth, or Wikipedia coverage.

salience:
Is the phrase between <target> tags central to the main information communicated in this text, so that it would be important in a concise summary? Judge textual importance/foregrounding, not whether the phrase is a valid event, whether an event record should be created, or whether Wikipedia contains it. Background details and incidental actions are not salient merely because they are concrete.

admission:
Under this fixed text-only policy, should this item be admitted to event organization? Admit when the body makes at least one identifiable real-world occurrence, action, change, result, institutional act, or explicit event reference one of its main pieces of information. A background event only used as an example or incidental support does not automatically qualify. Commentary, replies, old or small events and personal experiences can qualify. Abstract views, general properties, generic advice, and fictional plot evaluation alone do not qualify. Actual statements, arrangements, decisions and ongoing actions may qualify; wishes or conditional discussion do not establish that the proposed action happened. Do not require complete dates, places, names or a KB page. Do not verify truth or KB coverage. Use only the displayed body and metadata; do not read links, parent posts, quoted text or media. If this evidence is insufficient to support an organizing target, reject.
